first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A company that plans weddings in Portugal, with one advisor. Palaces and cliffs up top, which feels a bit grand for us, but the second line about marrying legally with at least one month ahead, and doing a symbolic one here and the legal bit at home, is the kind of thing I came for. The 'Check the rules for your passport' link is what I'd tap.

attention_map.quote: a legal wedding in Portugal for foreign couples starts at least one month ahead.
attention_map.why: Straight to the paperwork question. 'Sintra Palace' in the heading made me think big money and big crowds, but this line kept me.

attention_map.quote: How many guests? - Under 30 ... What are you celebrating? - Elopement
attention_map.why: First sign a group our size is actually expected. Seeing 'Elopement' as an option made me feel we're not an afterthought.

attention_map.quote: Planned by Wedded Concierge, with one Wedded Advisor from enquiry to the wedding weekend.
attention_map.why: Fine, one person to deal with is nice, but it says nothing new.

attention_map.quote: Romantic palaces in the Sintra hills that can be booked for a wedding
attention_map.why: Pretty, but this is history-lesson stuff. I scroll past looking for guest numbers and minimums and they aren't here.

I liked 'whether you are planning an elopement, a small wedding' and the nearest airport on every card. But the one line I scan for, guests, says the same non-answer five times. Does a palace even take 12 people?

attention_map.quote: state events can cancel bookings at Queluz or the National Palace of Sintra
attention_map.why: Useful that it's honest, but a palace isn't really us, and there's no word on whether a tiny group can book one.

attention_map.quote: A Catholic marriage is legally recognised on its own.
attention_map.why: Answers my religious ceremony question directly. The 'In the city' civil ceremony option also sounds simple and small.

attention_map.quote: fees may be charged either way, with a minimum.
attention_map.why: So there IS a minimum, and they're telling me it exists without telling me what it is. That's exactly what I'm worried about.

attention_map.quote: Witnesses are optional: two to four may take part.
attention_map.why: This is the best part for me. Documents, translations, witnesses, one month, six months, with government links. I finally get the steps. But it says the advisor 'walks you through', not that they do it for us.

attention_map.quote: What a wedding in Portugal costs depends on five things: your guest count, the region, the season...
attention_map.why: No number at all, not even a starting point. 'Your Wedded Advisor talks you through the options' means I find out on a call.

attention_map.quote: There is no set Portugal package.
attention_map.why: I wanted a small package. And the list, welcome dinner, late party, Sunday brunch, is a three-day production, which is the opposite of what we want.

attention_map.quote: Exclusive use can mean paying for rooms your guests do not fill
attention_map.why: Worry for a small group: if we take a quinta with 10 people, do we pay for 30 rooms? It raises the fear but doesn't settle it.

attention_map.quote: They walk you through the exact route to marry legally for your nationality, and check each venue contract for rooms, buy-outs, minimums and VAT before you sign.
attention_map.why: Good to have one person, and good they check minimums. Still 'walk you through', not 'we handle the documents and witnesses'.

attention_map.quote: Elopements and small weddings are welcome.
attention_map.why: This is the line I wanted near the top. The form is short enough to do on my phone, with Under 30 and Catholic as options.

attention_map.quote: Witnesses are optional in a Portuguese civil ceremony, so two of you can marry with no guests at all
attention_map.why: FAQ 9 is basically my question. Very reassuring, though the cost is just 'for a fee'.

attention_map.quote: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding
attention_map.why: Celebrity weddings are not relevant to us. Skipped.

questions_answered.question: Does this work for 30 guests or fewer, and is there a smaller package?
questions_answered.evidence: Small groups are welcomed: 'Under 30' guest option, 'whether you are planning an elopement, a small wedding', 'Elopements and small weddings are welcome', FAQ 9 'two of you can marry with no guests at all'. But no smaller package: 'There is no set Portugal package', and every region card says 'Guests: Ask your Wedded Advisor'.

questions_answered.question: Do you handle the legal side: documents, witnesses, registry?
questions_answered.evidence: The legal steps are laid out very clearly with official sources (documents, translations, 'Witnesses are optional: two to four may take part', one month minimum). But the company only says 'Your Wedded Advisor walks you through the exact route for your nationality'. Nothing says they gather the documents, book the registry or arrange witnesses for us.

questions_answered.question: What is the minimum spend?
questions_answered.evidence: Costs tab gives no figure: 'depends on five things'. The venue box confirms minimums exist ('fees may be charged either way, with a minimum') without saying what they are. Registry fee is just 'The civil registry charges a fee for the ceremony.'

questions_answered.question: Can we have a religious ceremony (for example Catholic) here?
questions_answered.evidence: 'A Catholic marriage is legally recognised on its own.' FAQ 3 repeats it, s6 lists 'civil, Catholic or symbolic', and the form has a Catholic ceremony option. It does not say how to arrange a church, but the answer is clear.

objections_triggered.objection: Minimum guest numbers or spend that don't fit a small group
objections_triggered.triggered_by: 'fees may be charged either way, with a minimum.' and 'Exclusive use can mean paying for rooms your guests do not fill', with no amount anywhere and 'Guests: Ask your Wedded Advisor' on every region

Mostly calmed by the step-by-step 'Marrying legally' tab with official links, but the Australian block ('Confirm with the Registo Civil or the Embassy of Portugal in Canberra which document you need') still leaves me doing the chasing myself

trust_signals_noticed: Clear legal steps with official government sources and 'Checked October 2026'
'Under 30' guest band and 'Elopement' option in the qualifier and form
'Elopements and small weddings are welcome.' in the form intro
FAQ 9 on small weddings and elopements
Nearest airport named on every region card
Advisor checks 'rooms, buy-outs, minimums and VAT before you sign'
turn_offs_noticed: Minimums hidden until the call: a minimum is mentioned but never stated, and costs have no figure
Big-production framing: palaces, 'three-day weekend', welcome dinner, late party, Sunday brunch, exclusive use

emotional_response.overall: Relieved about the legal side, uneasy about money
emotional_response.positive: Finally understand the paperwork, and the page does say small weddings are welcome
emotional_response.negative: Feels pitched at bigger weddings, and the one number I need is held back for a call

payload.decision_reason: Small groups are clearly welcome by the end and the legal steps are the clearest I've seen, so this goes on my list. But I still don't know if they actually do the paperwork and witnesses for us or just explain it, there's no small package, and they admit venues have minimums without saying what they are. I'll come back and compare before I fill in a form and wait for a call to hear the price.
payload.verbatim_reaction: OK, this actually explains the documents and witnesses properly, and 'Elopements and small weddings are welcome' is what I needed to hear. But it's palaces and three-day weekends everywhere, 'Guests: Ask your Wedded Advisor' on every region, and 'with a minimum' with no number. Do you handle the paperwork or just tell me about it? And what's the least we'd spend for 15 people? I'm saving it, not sending it yet.
